messages:
ash (oncall): noticing a spike of CUDA OOMs on decode nodes in eu-west-1 at ~12:07 UTC. streaming requests dropping, lots of `max_tokens` > 100k from a single client.

maria (sre): confirmed in metrics — per-node GPU used hits 99% then container restarts. Token generation tail looks unbounded.

cleo (runtime): logs show repeated decode loops + excessive kv growth. sample stack: ```
E CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at ./decode_kernel.cu:412
call stack: decode_loop -> vram_alloc -> kv_store_expand
payload id: f3a1c..
```

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-596333 (pager: ash). Severity: P1. Notifying oncall rotation.

ash (oncall): i'm paging infra to quiesce traffic to the affected pool. quick mitigation options?

maria (sre): immediate mitigations: 1) emergency rate-shed for the model route; 2) apply runtime override to enforce max_tokens=2048 for streaming endpoints; 3) isolate offending API key.

patrick (support): we have a high-volume customer with a recent deploy. sending them a soft block now and asking for payload samples.

jim (eng): can we hotpatch the header validation so ridiculous `max_tokens` headers are clamped at ingress?

cleo (runtime): yes — we can flip a config on the routing layer to clamp header values. i'll prepare the command.

cleo (runtime): command to flip (k8s config map): ```
kubectl patch cm routing-config -n redwood --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/max_tokens_clamp","value":2048}]'
```

maria (sre): rolling that to eu-west-1 now. applying canary to 3 nodes then full roll. watch telemetry. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Patch rollout started on namespace redwood (eu-west-1). canary: 3 nodes.

ash (oncall): also enabling quota backstop: per-key QPS 10 + token cap 10k for 5m window. executing policy push.

cleo (runtime): added a soft-fail fallback: if kv growth > threshold then route to cpu-fallback pool (slower) instead of crashing. pushing config change.

patrick (support): customer responded — they rolled out a test that sends huge prompt loops. we've asked them to pause and provided guidance. they've accepted temporary block.

maria (sre): telemetry update: OOM restarts dropped 80% within 7m of applying clamp + quota. some tail errors remain from long-lived streams established earlier.

ash (oncall): mitigation checklist: 1) clamp headers (done), 2) rate-shed & per-key limits (done), 3) isolate offending key (done), 4) restart flapping pods gracefully (in progress), 5) customer comms (patrick).

cleo (runtime): doing staggered restart of 12 flapping decode pods to clear fragmentation. command: ```
for p in $(kubectl get pods -n decode -l role=decode -o name | shuf | head -n 12); do kubectl rollout restart $p -n decode; sleep 6; done
```

maria (sre): note: avoid full pool drain at once — we saw memory fragmentation persist on immediate mass-restart earlier.

jim (eng): filed a follow-up PR to add server-side max_tokens enforcement and telemetry for token count per request: PR #4281.

ash (oncall): customer impact: approx 2% request drop rate for eu-west-1 between 12:07-12:20 UTC, peak error code 503 / decode OOM. billing and SLA impact likely minimal but support to follow up.

patrick (support): opened support ticket to the affected customer with summary + actions taken. asked for confirmation of pause and promised ETA for full restoration.

cleo (runtime): long-term actions: 1) ingress validation (PR in review), 2) better kv eviction for streaming, 3) per-route generation caps, 4) circuit-breaker that returns 429 instead of letting node OOM.

maria (sre): can we add an automatic quarantine rule: if a single API key generates more than X restarts in Y minutes, quarantine it automatically?

cleo (runtime): yes — adding to the circuit-breaker backlog. will instrument with a counter and action.

incident-bot: Severity downgraded to P2 at 12:36 UTC — main mitigations applied, customer paused, OOM restarts down to baseline.

ash (oncall): closing notes: short outage window ~12:07-12:36 UTC, root cause: unbounded generation from a client test combined with missing server-side max_tokens enforcement and KV growth behavior. follow-ups: see RFC ticket INF-1256 for detailed postmortem tasks assigned.

patrick (support): customer confirmed they paused and will add server-side checks. scheduled 1:1 to review rate limits.

jim (eng): leaving a note: consider quantized eviction for KV to reduce memory per entry; adding to infra roadmap.

maria (sre): filing post-incident report now, will include timeline, mitigations, comms, and next steps.

ash (oncall): thanks all. marking incident resolved but keep watch on eu-west-1 for 24h. :white_check_mark:
